akhfash:4-4.t:
He said ﴿فَظَلَّتْ أَعْنَاقُهُمْ لَهَا خَاضِعِينَ﴾: they claim that it refers to groups, as in "هذا عُنُقٌ من الناس" (this is a 'neck' of people), meaning "a great number". Or He used the masculine, as some feminine words are made masculine when annexed to a masculine. The poet said [in the ṭawīl metre; this is poetic witness no. 256]:
باكَرْتُهَا والدِّيكُ يَدْعُو صباحَهُ * إِذَا مَا بَنُو نَعْشٍ دَنَوْا فَتَصَوَّبُوا
(I came to it early, while the cock was calling its morning, when the Banū Naʿsh (the stars of the Bear) had drawn near and gone down.)
So the plural of this (عنق, a group) is "أَعْناقٌ". Or He used the masculine because of its annexation to the masculine, just as a word is made feminine because of its annexation to a feminine, as in his words [in the ṭawīl metre; this is poetic witness no. 257]:
وَتشْرَقُ بالقَوْلِ الذي قَدْ أَذَعْتَهُ * كَما شَرِقَتْ صَدْرُ القَنَاةِ مِنَ الدَّمِ
(And you choke on the word you have spread abroad, as the upper part of the spear choked with blood.)
Another said [in the rajaz metre; this is poetic witness no. 258]:
* لَمَا رَأَى مَتْنَ السَّمَاءِ انْقَدَّتِ *
(When he saw the expanse of the sky split open.)
And he said [in the ṭawīl metre; this is poetic witness no. 259]:
إِذَا القُنْبُضَاتُ طَوَّفْنَ بالضُّحى * رَقَدْنَ عَلَيْهِنَّ الحِجَالُ المُسَجَّفُ
(When the short women go about in the forenoon, these ones sleep with curtained canopies over them.)
"القُنْبُضُ" means the short one. Another said [in the ṭawīl metre; this is poetic witness no. 260]:
وإِنَّ امْرَءاً أَهْدَى إِلَيْكِ وَدُونَهُ * من الأَرْضِ مَوْمَاةٌ وبَيْداَءُ خَيْفَقُ
لمحْقُوقَةٌ أَنْ تَسْتَجيِبي لِصَوْتِهِ * وَأَنْ تَعْلَمِي أَنَّ المُعَانَ مُوَفَّقُ
(A man who sent a gift to you, with a waterless waste and a vast desert between you, is one to whom you are bound to respond to his call, and to know that the one who is helped is granted success.)
He used the feminine, though the one who has the claim is the man; he used the feminine only because of his words "أَنْ تَسْتَجِيبِي لِصَوْتِهِ" (that you respond to his call). They say: "بَنَاتُ عُرْسٍ" (weasels), "بَنَاتُ نَعْشٍ" and "بَنُو نَعْشٍ" (the stars of the Bear). A woman of the Arabs said: "أَنَا امْرُؤُ لا أُحِبُ الشَرَّ" (I am a man (masc.) who does not love evil). A man was mentioned to Ruʾba, and he said: "كانَ أَحَدَ بناتِ مَساجِدِ اللهِ" (he was one of the daughters of the mosques of Allah), as though he made him a pebble.

akhfash:16-16.t: And He said ﴿إِنَّا رَسُولُ رَبِّ ٱلْعَالَمِينَ﴾: this seems to be like "العَدُوّ" (enemy); you say "هما عَدُوٌّ لي" (the two of them are an enemy to me).

akhfash:22-22.t: And He said ﴿وَتِلْكَ نِعْمَةٌ تَمُنُّهَا عَلَيّ﴾: it is said that this is a question, as though he said "Is that a favour you remind me of?". Then he explained it, saying ﴿أَنْ عَبَّدتَّ بَنِي إِسْرَائِيلَ﴾, and made it a badal (substitute) for "the favour".

akhfash:72-72.t:
And He said ﴿هَلْ يَسْمَعُونَكُمْ﴾, i.e. "do they hear from you?" or "do they hear your supplication?". He omitted "the supplication", as the poet said [in the basīṭ metre; this is poetic witness no. 261]:
القائدُ الخَيْلَ مَنْكُوباً دَوابِرُها * قَدْ أُحْكِمَتْ حَكَماتُ القِدِّ والأَبَقا
(The one who leads the horses with worn-down hooves, the bridle-rings of rawhide and of flax having been made fast.)
You mean: "the bridle-rings of flax were made fast"; he omitted "حَكَماتِ" (bridle-rings) and put "الأَبَقَ" in its place. "الأَبَقُ" is flax.

akhfash:197-197.t: And He said ﴿أَوَ لَمْ يَكُن لَّهُمْ آيَةً أَن يَعْلَمَهُ﴾: (أن يعلمه) is a noun in the position of the nominative, like ﴿مَّا كَانَ حُجَّتَهُمْ إِلاَّ أَن قَالُواْ﴾. But in this only the accusative is possible for the first (آية); ﴿أَن يَعْلَمَهُ﴾ is what is the sign. The nominative is allowed, but it is weak.

akhfash:198-198.t: And He said ﴿عَلَىٰ بَعْضِ ٱلأَعْجَمِينَ﴾: its singular is "الأَعْجَمُ" (the non-Arab), and it is a relational (nisba) form, like "الأَشْعَرِين".

akhfash:201-203.t:
And He said ﴿لاَ يُؤْمِنُونَ بِهِ حَتَّىٰ يَرَوُاْ ٱلْعَذَابَ ٱلأَلِيمَ﴾: ﴿فَيَأْتِيَهُم﴾ is not conjoined to (what follows) ﴿حَتَّىٰ﴾; it is only an answer to His word ﴿لاَ يُؤْمِنُونَ بِهِ﴾, and since it is an answer to the negation it is accusative. Likewise ﴿فَيَقُولُواْ﴾ is only an answer to the negation.
And He said ﴿إِنِّيۤ آمَنتُ بِرَبِّكُمْ فَٱسْمَعُونِ﴾, i.e. so listen to me. «[Translator's note: this verse is Q 36:25; it appears here as written in the source.]»
